summary: I built the largest-files list as designed. `LargestFiles.Top(ScanStore, int)` in the new src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis folder makes one pass over the store into a bounded min-heap on (ChargedOnDisk, ChargedSize, -index) and reads only charged values. The outcome panel now has a section headed "Largest files, by space on disk" with a caption and a virtualized, wrapping ListBox of 100 rows. It is filled last in ShowOutcome and hidden when a scan starts and in ShowProblem. The report gains largestFilesShown, largestFileOnDisk and largestFilesMs, plus window keys for the section, caption, list and unreadable expander. For M2, ScanStore.Size and ScanStore.OnDisk are now internal. The architecture rule is twinned (an xUnit Fact plus a fitness.yaml entry above the settled marker, parity AGREE), and plant rows F17–F19 fire in both engines. Results: Core 166/166 (10 new tests), all 20 default window cases pass (5 new, L-001 to L-005), and harness rows F17–F19 AS-RECORDED. Two things are not done: the second-scan case (C-009, O-011) went to validate's drive list under M3, and the real C:\ largestFilesMs reading is also validate's (m5).

files.why: LargestFiles.Top and the LargestFile record: a bounded-heap top-N over charged sizes, largest first, with each row's path from GetPath. This is the first Scan Analysis code.
M2: Size and OnDisk are now internal, so the compiler keeps the App and every later project to ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk. The remark saying reads are public was updated.

New LargestFilesPanel section: header, caption, column headings and a ListBox that virtualizes, has horizontal scrolling disabled, stretches its items and wraps the path (m1). It fills the space left in the panel. UnreadableExpander is now docked at the bottom, and UnreadableList has MaxHeight 200.

ShowLargestFiles runs after all existing outcome content (m7). It times Top into LargestFilesMs and builds the m4 caption, covering the stopped and unreadable cases and the 'No non-empty files found' text. HideLargestFiles runs at scan start and in ShowProblem (M3). Also adds the LargestFileRow type and the constant 100.

Schema-1 additive keys: top-level largestFilesShown, largestFileOnDisk and largestFilesMs; window keys LargestFilesPanel{visible,actualHeight}, LargestFilesCaption, LargestFilesList{actualHeight,inView,realizedRows} and UnreadableExpander{visible,actualHeight,inView}. inView is a layout-slot check measured against a layout mutant.

Nine real-tree Facts: depth, cap with ties at the cut, empty trees, hardlink, links, sparse, odd paths, a cancelled scan and an unreadable folder. Also a scale Fact over 4,417,469 synthetic entries that checks correctness and allocation of about 26 KB.
xUnit twin of the rule: TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore over src/FsAnalyser.Core/Analysis/*.cs (m6).

m6: the engine-appended settled SL-040 entry is replaced by a twinned entry above the marker. It has (?m), including_comments: true and the Fact-named scope. It sits before TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls, which RuleCases treats as the last twinned entry.

Plant rows F17 (the real raw-size line from Scanner.cs:267), F18 (the real File.Delete line from App.xaml.cs:66) and F19 (a comment naming File.Exists). All must fire in both engines. The row note was updated from 27 to 30.

Cases L-001 to L-005: report scalars and a missing root, the unreadable-folder caption, 100 rows with an unpaired-surrogate first row next to a filled unreadable list, the empty-list caption, and the stopped-scan caption (hooked). Also the Deny-Listing and Undo-DenyListing helpers using icacls on this user's own temp folders.

The hard-coded parity and harness counts now match the added Fact: 8 facts, 11 twinned entries, 23 patterns, -ExpectFacts 8 and 9, and 'xunit 8 Facts'. The settled counts, 7 and 8, were already stale at HEAD, which has 15 settled entries; they are now 15 and 16.

obligations.how: LargestFilesTests.RanksFilesAtAnyDepthAndNeverAFolder has a 3 MiB file six folders down, a 2 MiB file at the top, and a folder holding 5 x 1 MiB (5 MiB total). The deep file ranks first, the folder is never listed, and every row is a File in rank order. Passed.

LargestFilesTests.KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut uses 95 distinct sizes and 10 tied files at the cut, with count 100. It checks exactly 100 rows, no duplicate paths, and that the tied files kept are the five lowest store indices (scan order is deterministic per m3/M1). The result equals a full sort's first 100. Passed.

WindowCases L-004 scans a tree of zero-length files and an empty folder. The app shows the caption 'No non-empty files found.' with no rows; the report has largestFilesShown 0 and largestFileOnDisk null, and the list is not in view. Passed. The Core half is LargestFilesTests.ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList, which also covers count 0, a negative count and a null store; passed.

LargestFilesTests.AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce has a 3 MiB file with a second hardlink in another folder. The second name is confirmed as HardlinkDuplicate, and the list is exactly [first name at 3 MiB, the other file]. Passed.

LargestFilesTests.NoRowComesFromALink creates a file symlink, a folder symlink and a junction through TempTree, which fails loudly and never skips (Q-001). All three are recorded as Link, and the list is only the target file. Passed.

LargestFilesTests.RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes has a 64 MiB sparse file with nothing allocated next to a dense 1 MiB file. The order is dense then sparse, and the sparse row has ChargedSize 64 MiB and on-disk of 4 KiB or less. With count 1, only the dense file is kept. Passed.

LargestFilesTests.EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath checks a path over 260 characters, a name ending in a dot, one ending in a space, and 'a'+U+D800+'b.bin'. Each row's Path equals the created string exactly, contains no U+FFFD, and File.Exists('\\?\'+path) is true. Passed.

WindowCases L-005 presses Stop mid-scan through the hook. The report shows Cancelled, the list built from the partial store, and a caption ending 'in the part read before the scan stopped.' that matches OutcomeDetail's file count. Passed, with 2 rows. LargestFilesTests.AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead covers the Core side: only f0's and f1's files are listed. The 'settles the writer-join invariant' part is by construction, not by test, per the M1 override: Scanner.cs:12 scans on the caller's thread, the canceller is joined in the Dispose of `using var io` (Scanner.cs:35), and ShowOutcome runs after the awaited task (MainWindow.xaml.cs:151).

Not built as a test. The M3 disposition put 'a second scan, including one that fails, clears and hides the previous list' on validate's drive list, because the hook has only stop/throw/close modes and report mode counts only the first ending (App.xaml.cs:104-105). The code side is built: StartScan calls HideLargestFiles before any progress, and ShowProblem calls it too. L-001's missing-root run shows that a failed ending leaves the section hidden, with largestFilesMs null, but only for a first scan. Making this a window case needs a new hook mode that starts a second scan, which I listed as a follow-up.

WindowCases L-002 puts the biggest file (2 MiB) inside a folder denied list access with icacls, beside readable 128 KiB and 64 KiB files. largestFileOnDisk is 131072, and the caption reads 'Top 2 of 2 files scanned. Files in 1 unreadable folder are not included.' Passed. The Core half is LargestFilesTests.AFileInAFolderTheScanCouldNotReadIsNotListed.

WindowCases L-003 has 105 files, the largest named 'a'+U+D800+'b-...', plus a denied folder. The app exits 0 with the report written, so drawing row 0 did not throw. It shows 100 rows with only 7 realized, so the list virtualizes, and both LargestFilesList and UnreadableExpander are inView at the default 880x600 window. Passed. A layout mutant (the design's list docked on top with a fixed MaxHeight) makes this case fail with UnreadableExpander actualHeight 0.

WindowCases L-001 scans a planted tree with files at three depths and one empty file. It checks largestFilesShown 3, largestFileOnDisk 327680 against the tree, a non-null largestFilesMs, the panel visible and laid out, the caption 'Top 3 of 4 files scanned.', 3 rows realized, and no 'plantedname' anywhere in the report (Q-016). A second run on a missing root gives 0, null, null and the panel hidden. eng/read-window.ps1 needed no change: it prints raw JSON and ConvertFrom-Json accepts the new keys. Passed.

LargestFilesScaleTests.RanksAStoreOfFourMillionEntriesInOnePassWithoutCollectingIt builds a 4,417,469-entry store (3,533,091 files) with planted top 100. Decoy links, hardlink duplicates and folders are larger and charged nothing. The test asserts the exact planted set, the ranking, and under 1 MiB allocated by Top (measured 26,400 bytes). Top took 19.9 ms in Release and 194 ms in Debug. The real C:\ largestFilesMs against the 100 ms threshold is validate's (m5). Passed.

A grep of src for raw Size(/OnDisk( found only Scanner.cs:267-268 in Core, plus Core.Tests through InternalsVisibleTo; nothing in the App. ScanStore.Size and OnDisk are now internal and the ScanStore remark is updated. The Analysis/** regex stays for code inside Core. Build is clean and all 166 tests pass.

Following the report's x:Name convention that the M3 disposition named, the visibility scalar is window.LargestFilesPanel.visible (with actualHeight), read after the fill and asserted in L-001 to L-005. ShowProblem also hides the section. The second-scan check is for validate's named drive list (see O-011). I cannot edit that list, so it is recorded in not_built and follow_ups.
LargestFilesList sets ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Disabled", its ItemContainerStyle sets HorizontalContentAlignment=Stretch, and the path TextBlock uses TextWrapping="Wrap".

L-003 plants the unpaired-surrogate file as the largest, so it is row 0 and realized. The report is written after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded), which follows the fill and render. The run exits 0 with a report, so WPF drew the lone surrogate without throwing.

The caption is 'Top {n} of {files} files scanned[ in the part read before the scan stopped].' and the empty text is 'No non-empty files found[...].'. A ' Files in {n} unreadable folder(s) are not included.' suffix is added when needed. L-001, L-002, L-003, L-004 and L-005 assert these.

The threshold is the one the disposition set: largestFilesMs over 100 on the real C:\ scan moves Top to Task.Run. The report carries largestFilesMs as fractional milliseconds from the one Top call, for validate to record. Build's own measurement at 4,417,469 synthetic entries is 19.9 ms in Release (the shipped configuration) and 194 ms in Debug.

The accessor shape is confirmed as a method call (ScanStore.cs:71/74), so neither pattern changed. The entry moved above the settled marker as 'TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore (*.cs)' with (?m) and including_comments: true, twinned by a new xUnit Fact. rules-parity AGREEs under both shells (8 facts, 11 twinned, 23 patterns). Plant rows use real lines: F17 is `_bytes += size - _store.Size(charged);` from Scanner.cs:267, F18 is `File.Delete(report);` from App.xaml.cs:66, and F19 is a comment. The harness against taad_v3's Fitness shows a CLEAN baseline and all three AS-RECORDED in both engines. The Analysis code's comments name none of the banned APIs.
ShowLargestFiles(result) is called after the UnreadableExpander block and before OutcomePanel is made visible and EndingShown is raised, so the report still follows the fill.

deviations: Layout. The design said the section sits above the unreadable list and gives the ListBox a fixed MaxHeight. Built that way, it pushes the unreadable list out, which is the C-011 failure. I built and measured the design-literal layout as a mutant: section docked on top with ListBox MaxHeight 240, expander as the fill child. At the default 880x600 window with 100 rows and one unreadable folder, UnreadableExpander read visible with actualHeight 0. So the section is now the fill child: its list takes exactly the space left, stays bounded and scrolls inside the panel. UnreadableExpander is docked at the bottom, still below the list, and is measured first. UnreadableList gets MaxHeight 200 so that, when expanded, it cannot take all the space. L-003 passes on the built layout and fails on the mutant.

Report keys. M3's 'largestFilesVisible' is window.LargestFilesPanel.visible (with actualHeight), following the x:Name convention that the M3 disposition itself cited. I added more window keys than the design named: LargestFilesCaption, LargestFilesList{actualHeight,inView,realizedRows} and UnreadableExpander{visible,actualHeight,inView}. With them, C-010 (the caption) and C-011 (virtualization and push-off) are checked by window cases instead of being left only to a person at validate. All are additive under schema 1, and none holds a name or a path.

inView. My first version checked the control's bounds against OutcomePanel. The layout mutant showed that check was blind, because a control squeezed out of a DockPanel keeps IsVisible with actualHeight 0 and has a zero-height slot. It now requires a non-zero ActualHeight, and that the control and each ancestor up to the Window are no larger than their layout slot minus margins. I verified that this version catches the mutant.

Rule name and placement. The design's rule is named 'the analysis code reads sizes only as the store charged them, and only from the store'. Per the m6 disposition it became the twinned entry 'TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore (*.cs)', named after its xUnit Fact as the fitness.yaml header requires, with the patterns unchanged. It sits above TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls, not directly above the marker, because a RuleCases C-003 shape assumes NoBcl is the last twinned entry.

tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1. I updated the counts my Fact changes: facts 7 to 8, twinned 10 to 11, patterns 21 to 23, and the ExpectFacts values. In the same lines I corrected the settled counts, 7 to 15 and 8 to 16. Those were already wrong at HEAD, which has 15 settled entries (SL-023/024: 4, SL-031: 3, SL-033: 3, SL-038: 5), so C-001 and C-003 were failing before this slice.

LargestFiles.Top keeps the ScanStore signature, per the M1 override. Its doc comment corrects the design's 'multithreaded' wording: the index follows the single-threaded depth-first scan (Scanner.cs:12), so tied membership at the cut is deterministic.
not_built: A test for C-009, 'start another scan' (a second scan, or a failed one, after a list has been shown). Per the M3 disposition this belongs on validate's drive list: 'a second scan, including one that fails, clears and hides the previous list'. The hook has only stop/throw/close modes, and report mode records only the first ending. The code clears the list at StartScan and in ShowProblem. Only the first-scan failure (L-001, missing root) is machine-checked.
The real C:\ largestFilesMs measurement against the 100 ms threshold (m5). That is validate's; build measured a synthetic store of 4,417,469 entries instead.

The validate-time visual checks the design assigns to a person driving the exe: how rows look (both sizes, wrapped long paths) and how the lone-surrogate glyph renders. That it renders without a crash is covered by L-003.
The design's open questions are unchanged: ranking stays on on-disk size (with logical shown), pagefile/hiberfil/swapfile are unlabelled, and the count is fixed at 100.
follow_ups: Add a hook mode (for example 'rescan') that, in interactive mode, waits for the first ending, logs LargestFilesPanel's state, starts a second scan and logs again. That would turn C-009 into a window case instead of a validate drive item.
At validate, read largestFilesMs from a real C:\ scan. If it is over 100 ms, move only the Top call in ShowLargestFiles to Task.Run and keep the fill before EndingShown.

tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 hard-codes the parity counts and assumes TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls is the last twinned entry. Every new twinned rule has to edit it. Deriving the counts, or anchoring its shapes on a named entry, would remove that coupling.
RuleCases C-008 still runs only F01-F16. F17-F19 run only in a full harness run (`--scenario plants`) or with `--only F17,F18,F19`. Consider adding them to a RuleCases case.
The design's deferred Desktop UI items for this list: open in Explorer, copy path, and a live list during a scan.

tests.note: Bootstrapped SDK 10.0.401 into the gitignored .dotnet/ (Q-003). There is no machine-wide 10.0 SDK here.
4,417,469 entries: Top(100) took 19.9 ms in Release and allocated 26,400 bytes. Debug gave 193.8 ms and 26,440 bytes.
166/166 on the final tree, including ArchitectureRulesTests (8 Facts) and RuleCopiesAgreeTests.
AGREE: 8 facts, 11 twinned entries, 23 patterns, 15 settled.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case L-003 (with the design-literal layout mutant applied temporarily, then restored and hash-verified)
tests.note: Intended evidence. With the first inView the mutant PASSED, which showed that check was blind. After the fix the mutant FAILS on 'UnreadableExpander is inside the panel' (actualHeight 0). MainWindow.xaml was restored to hash 2445012F...
20 passed: C-001 to C-014, O-016 and L-001 to L-005. L-003 realized 7 of 100 rows; L-005 stopped with 2 rows. N-001 to N-004 not run (they need -IncludeNetwork).
Run twice, before and after the yaml reorder. Clean baseline CLEAN (xUnit 8 Facts, Fitness pass, 26 rules, none unmatched). F17, F18 and F19 fire/fire, AS-RECORDED, no stray hits.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (then C-003 and C-004), first run
tests.note: Before updating the counts, the hard-coded '7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns' strings failed; the settled counts were already stale at HEAD. After the update, C-003 failed once because the new entry followed NoBcl. Fixed by moving the entry.
All five parity cases pass on the final tree.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-007 / C-008 -EnginePython <engine python> -EngineRoot C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend
tests.note: C-007: clean scenario, 'xunit 8 Facts'. C-008: 16 must-fire rows AS-RECORDED, and both bites give the new counts.
Checks the reported single-test command form with a build: 1/1.
